blocks.heading: Protecting the environment
blocks.text: Government can protect against pollution through standards, monitoring, enforcement, information and incentives for cleaner methods. It can protect non-renewable resources through extraction limits, conditions, conservation and incentives to use materials efficiently. The measure must affect the actual mechanism and be capable of implementation. A rule without monitoring may change little; an excessive or poorly targeted burden can create costs without proportionate benefit. Distinguish reducing ongoing emissions from conserving a finite resource stock. Planting trees does not replace extracted mineral deposits.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: A hypothetical producer discharges waste while another extracts a limited mineral resource. Pollution controls address the discharge; extraction and conservation measures address depletion. Different problems need different measures rather than one generic environmental slogan.

blocks.heading: Protection against pollution
blocks.text: Pollution protection can set acceptable discharge or emission conditions, require effective control, monitor compliance and apply consequences or incentives. Explain how a measure changes behaviour or reduces the stated harm. Costs and practical enforcement matter. A charge may encourage reduction where a cleaner option exists, while a standard may be needed to secure a particular result. These are general policy options, not statements of a current legal rule or rate.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: A hypothetical workshop can contain its dust using a suitable maintained filter. A monitored dust-control condition targets the source. Merely publishing a rule without checking equipment performance would give weaker assurance.

blocks.heading: Protection of non-renewable resources
blocks.text: Non-renewable resources such as mineral deposits are finite on human time scales. Protection can limit extraction, require suitable use and restoration arrangements and encourage resource efficiency, recycling or alternatives. Restoration can reduce site damage but does not recreate the mineral stock already extracted. Balance current useful output against future availability and environmental consequences using the facts.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: A hypothetical enterprise seeks to extract a finite local mineral deposit rapidly. Extraction conditions and efficiency measures can limit depletion and waste. A pollution filter alone would not decide how much of the stock is removed.
